fields.meaning: Fellow …, … with each other (友達同士)
examples: We went on a trip together as a group of friends.
We're next-door neighbors, so we often talk.
Don't butt into a conversation between us women.

fields.meaning: On the contrary…, on the other hand…
fields.connection: V plain form + 反面 / N・Na + である / Na + な / Aい
examples: Cities are convenient, but on the other hand, prices are high.
This medicine works well, but on the other hand, its side effects are strong.
He is serious, but on the other hand, he is inflexible.
Working from home gives you freedom, but on the other hand, managing yourself is difficult.
She is shy with strangers, but on the other hand, she is very outgoing with people she is close to.
Convenient, but on the other hand
fields.explain:
Neutral nuance, analytical/objective evaluation.
Suitable for written language, reports and presentations; also natural in conversation when comparing two sides.
Not used with a command/volition in the second clause; focuses on describing facts/characteristics.

• Expresses two opposite sides/a trade-off of the same thing/matter: “on the other hand / conversely”.
• Usually states one advantage together with one disadvantage (or vice versa), keeping the evaluation balanced.
• The subject A of both clauses should be the same, to ensure “two sides of the same target”.
fields.notes:
• When the subjects are different, prefer ～一方で/～に対して over ～反面.
• In formal writing, Nである反面 makes the sentence concise and precise.
• Softer alternatives in conversation: その一方で/でも.
meaning_vi: 「～だが、逆に…の面もある。」あることの対比的な両面を言うときに使う。
~ but conversely there is also the side of…
Used to express two opposite sides of a certain issue.
examples: 1. 都会の生活は面白いことが多い反面、ストレスも多い。
City life has many interesting things, but there is also a lot of stress.
2. 一人旅は気楽な反面、何でも一人でやらなければならないので、不便だ。
Traveling alone is carefree, but it is inconvenient because you have to do everything by yourself.
3. 仕事を辞めて自由な時間が増えた反面、緊張感もなくなってしまった。
Quitting my job gave me more free time, but on the other hand, I also lost the sense of tension I needed. | Also written 半面
mistakes: Using it for two different subjects: X 東京は便利な反面、田舎は不便だ → use ～に対して/～一方で instead.
Second clause is a request/volition: X 便利な反面、我慢しましょう → does not fit the descriptive nuance.
Confusing the sequence with a simple “but”: ～が/けれども does not necessarily mean “two sides”.

fields.meaning: As long as…, then…
examples: As long as I have time, I'll help.
As long as you're here, I'm not afraid.
As long as you prepare, it isn't difficult.
As long as you've let them know, it's fine even if you're late.
This medicine works well as long as you take it after meals.
As long as the price is low, it will sell in large quantities.
fields.explain:
Emphasizes a minimum condition, with a slight feeling of “that's enough”.
The original particle of N (が/を/は) is usually omitted before さえ: お金 さえ あれば (you do not say お金 がさえ …).
B can be a command/volition/advice:早く連絡し さえすれば、間に合うよ。
Avoid using it when A and B are logically contradictory (A is the minimum sufficient condition, yet B is a total negation).

• “As long as … then …”; emphasizes a minimum condition; when it is met, the desired result will occur.
• “さえ” means “even/only need”; combined with “～ば” it forms a minimum sufficient condition.
• V-てさえいれば emphasizes a state that has been secured in advance or throughout a period of time.
• Used in inference, advice and stating principles; B usually does not contradict A.
fields.notes:
• Irregular verbs: する→しさえすれば；来る→来さえすれば（きさえすれば）.
• V-てさえいれば is suitable when the condition needs to be maintained over time: 連絡してさえいれば安心だ。
• If you want to emphasize “it is very unlikely to happen without A”, you can add さえ: これさえあれば十分だ。
meaning_vi: Indicates that if a condition is met, that alone is enough.
examples: 1. ①　熱さえ下がれば
As long as the fever goes down...
2. ②　恋人の声さえ聞ければと思って、電話をした。
I called just to hear my partner's voice.
3. ③　あの問題さえわかれば、合格したと思う。
I think I would have passed if only I had understood that question.
4. ➃　だれかに道を聞きさえすれば、間に合ったのに。
If only I had asked someone the way, I would have made it in time.
meaning_vi: 「～が実現すれば、それだけで…が実現する。」「～さえ～ば（なら）」は…が成り立つための必要最低限の条件を示す。
If ~ is realized, then with that alone … will be realized.
～さえ～ば（なら） indicates the minimum condition that needs to be met…
examples: 1. 太郎は漫画さえ読んでいれば退屈しないようだ。
Taro seems not to get bored as long as he is reading manga.
2. 体さえ丈夫ならどんなことにも挑戦できる。
As long as you are physically healthy, you can take on any challenge.
3. 一言「ごめんなさい。」と言いさえすれば、相手は許してくれるだろう。
As long as you just say 「I'm sorry.」, the other person will probably forgive you.
meaning_vi: それだけで→後(うし)ろのことが成立(せいりつ)する
As long as, if only
examples: 1. あとは肉さえ焼けば、夕食の準備は終わりだ。
Now all that's left is to grill the meat, and dinner will be ready.
2. あの子は暇さえあればいつも本を読んでいる。
That child is always reading whenever there is free time.
3. 元気さえ良かったら、山頂までいきたっかたのだが・・・・・。
If only the weather had been good, I would have wanted to go up to the summit...
4. この国では、まじめに働きさえすれば生活に困ることはない。
In this country, as long as you work hard, you will not have trouble making a living.
5. あなたと私が黙ってさえいれば（/黙っていさえすれば）、このことはだれにもわからないだろう。
As long as you and I keep quiet, no one will find out about this.
6. 道が込んでさえいなければ10分ぐらいで着くだろう。
As long as the roads aren't congested, we'll get there in about 10 minutes.
7. 「あまり辛いさえなければ何でもいただきます」
As long as it isn't too spicy, I can eat anything.
8. 「体が丈夫でさえあれば、もっと働きたいですが」
If only I were physically healthy, I would like to work more, but...
9. このコンテストは、２０歳以上でさえあればだれでも参加できる。
Anyone can enter this contest as long as they are 20 or older.
explain: Expresses that as long as there is ～, the following state will be established.
examples: 1. 携帯電話を買った。これさえあれば、時計もカメラもいらない。
I bought a cell phone. As long as I have this, I need neither a watch nor a camera.
2. この薬を飲みさえすれば、すぐに治ります。
As long as you take this medicine, you'll get better right away.
mistakes: Keeping the original particle: お金がさえあれば × → お金さえあれば ✓
Confusing it with “さえ” meaning “even”, which does not go with “ば”: 彼さえ来た（even he came）≠ a condition.
Using it with an adjective without “ある/状態”: 高いさえあれば × → 安くさえあれば（with ある）.
B contradicts A: お金さえあれば、買わない × (illogical) → お金さえあれば、買える ✓

fields.meaning: Perhaps because…, probably due to… (せいか)
fields.connection: V/A plain form + せいか / Nの/Naな + せいか
examples: Maybe it's my age, but I get tired easily these days.
Probably from lack of sleep, I have a headache.
Perhaps because it rained, there are few customers today.

fields.meaning: If you ask whether… (actually, not necessarily); the reason is that
examples: If you ask whether all Japanese people are good at kanji, that's not really the case.
The reason he was chosen is that he has a lot of experience.
If you ask whether expensive things are always good, that is not necessarily so.

fields.meaning: On a par with…, along with…
examples: Kyoto, along with Nara, is a city with a long history.
Mount Fuji, along with cherry blossoms, is said to be a symbol of Japan.
Soccer, along with baseball, is a popular sport.

fields.meaning: Suited to…, in line with…
examples: I change the way I speak to match the other person's level.
Let's dance to the music.
I want to find a job that suits me.

fields.meaning: Corresponds to…, is… (彼は私のおじに当たる)
examples: He is my mother's younger brother, which makes him my uncle.
This year marks the 50th anniversary of the founding.

fields.meaning: Needless to say…, of course…
examples: Needless to say, he passed.
It goes without saying that health is important.
It goes without saying that practice is necessary.

fields.meaning: Is set as…, is currently… (objective)
fields.connection: N + となっている / [rule・state] + となっている
examples: In this building, smoking is not permitted on the premises.
The application deadline is the end of this month.
Admission is 500 yen for adults.

fields.meaning: The former…, the latter… (written language)
examples: Of trains and buses, the former are fast, while the latter are cheap.
There are Plan A and Plan B; the former is expensive, and the latter offers fewer services.
Of kanji and hiragana, the former came from China, and the latter was created in Japan.

fields.meaning: Not necessarily…, not always…
fields.connection: 必ずしも + V/A/N plain form + ～ない（とは限らない・わけではない）
examples: Expensive things are not necessarily good.
Even if you graduate from a famous university, it doesn't necessarily mean you will succeed.
You can't say that his opinion is necessarily right.

fields.meaning: …point, in terms of… (この点, ～という点で)
fields.connection: V plain form + 点 / Nの点 / Naな点 / Aい点 / ～という点で
examples: That plan has problems in terms of cost.
In terms of safety, this car is highly rated.
The two proposals are the same in that they both take time.

fields.meaning: First of all, firstly…; besides
examples: First of all, health is important.
Please think about safety first and speed second.
I don't want to go, and besides, I have no money.

fields.meaning: Suffix 型: type, form, size… (最新型)
examples: I bought the latest model of smartphone.
My blood type is A.
This factory makes small machines.

fields.meaning: Has… (classical Japanese, old form of ある in written language/advertisements)
fields.connection: N + あり（classical Japanese: 経験あり・条件あり）
examples: We are looking for people with "experience".
This apartment is convenient because it has parking.
This sale has conditions, so please read carefully.

fields.meaning: To influence, determine… (success or failure)
examples: Sometimes the weather influences the outcome of a game.
First impressions determine the relationship that follows.
This decision will probably determine the company's future.

fields.meaning: Unthinkable/unimaginable; unacceptable (考えられない)
fields.connection: plain form + とは + 考えられない

fields.meaning: To be related (to …) (関係がある)
(A) is precisely (the content describing A); (A) means … / (A) that is, …
Whether … or not … (the result is the same)
examples: Whether you submit this report or not, it will have no effect at all on your grade.
Whether everyone participates or not, I'll reserve a seat for each person just in case.
If it's only for about a day, whether you eat or not, your weight won't change much.
fields.explain: Using a form like 「…してもしなくても」, lists conditions in an affirmative–negative relationship and expresses that the result does not change in either case.

fields.meaning: To be (…) — the written/formal form of 「だ・です」
Expresses necessity, obligation
examples: There was no need to say it so harshly.
A grown adult surely needn't cry over something that minor.
A phone call or a letter will take care of it, so there's probably no need to go all the way there.
fields.explain: Used to state a critical judgment that an action is inappropriate, or a judgment that an action is unnecessary. It is a stiff, written-language expression; in spoken language, 「Ｖ－ることもないだろう」 is used more often.

fields.meaning: The thing/person that … is … (emphasizes the chosen part)
fields.connection: [plain form]のは ～ N/[plain form] + のほうだ

fields.meaning: Also …, … too …
Isn't it …?, … right? (conjecture/confirmation, casual tone)
examples: That person, isn't that Mr. Yamada?
Look, you're blushing. You like Yamada, don't you?
That's pretty good, isn't it? I don't think it's bad.
The keys? Aren't they on the table?
Sato? Hasn't he already gone home?
fields.explain: A casual form of 「のではないか」. Spoken with rising intonation. As in 2., 「んじゃないの」 is also possible. Men also use 「んじゃないか」. The polite form is 「んじゃありません」

fields.meaning: ～がた (polite plural suffix for people, as in あなたがた) means ～がた is a polite plural suffix used to refer respectfully to mul
fields.explain:
～がた (polite plural suffix for people, as in あなたがた) means ～がた is a polite plural suffix used to refer respectfully to multiple people, similar to 'you all' or 'ladies and gentlemen' in English.

Structure: Noun + がた

The suffix ～がた is attached to a noun referring to people (often pronouns or titles) to form a polite plural. It is more respectful and formal than the casual plural suffix ～たち. For example, あなたがた means 'you (plural)' in a polite manner. It is commonly used in formal or polite speech and writing.

fields.meaning: Expresses an extreme degree
examples: He stood up and looked around.
As soon as she got home, my younger sister ran straight up the stairs and dashed into her room.
She pushed her rivals aside and rose to stardom.
The political science professor's hairline has receded far up his forehead.
A plan came up for all of us to go to a hot spring during winter break.
Because too few people had signed up for the tour, they decided to allow families to join, and the number of participants swelled to more than double, leaving the travel agency in trouble.
fields.explain: Attaches to the continuative form (連用形) of a verb and expresses an action or movement in an upward direction, or a state of facing upward. 5. ～⑧ are figurative expressions in the upward sense.

fields.meaning: Expresses inference
examples:
Ａ: It's certain that a big hotel will be built nearby.
Ｂ: If so, the employment rate in this town might go up.

Ａ: This photo was taken in Kyoto in the summer.
Ｂ: If so, that means he was in Japan last July.
fields.explain: Used at the beginning of a sentence to state the speaker's conjecture or judgment based on what the other person has said. It means 「そのような事実・現状から考えると」 ("judging from such facts/the current situation"). It is close to 「それなら」, but 「だとすれば」 is somewhat more formal and is also used in written language. There are also 「そうだとすれば」「だとすると」「そうだとすると」, etc. （２００）

fields.meaning: Expresses a condition (hypothetical condition)
examples: I think that, from the husband's point of view, he would have many complaints about a wife who neglects the housework.
For him, as the person directly involved, it's not something he can decide that easily.
I think it's natural for a teacher to pay attention to the students who do well.
fields.explain: Takes a noun referring to a person and expresses the meaning 「その人の立場から見れば／考えれば」 ("seen/thought of from that person's standpoint"). Somewhat written in style. In spoken language, 「にしたら／にしてみれば」 is often used. （３４２）

examples: My father will attend in place of my mother, who has suddenly fallen ill.
There is a prediction that in the 21st century, Asian countries will take over from the existing developed countries as world leaders, but it must be said that there are still many unknowns.
fields.explain: A formal, written-language way of saying 「…にかわって」.

examples: According to this record, the castle was completed at the end of the 11th century.
According to him, this tea bowl is a highly valuable antique.

fields.name: ～向き（direction）
examples: Rooms facing south are bright and warm.
Please place it facing right.
Please lie on your side.
We would like to consider it positively.
fields.explain: Attaches to nouns indicating direction, such as compass directions (east, west, south, north), front/back/left/right, and up/down, and expresses facing in that direction. 4. is the idiomatic expression 「前向きに」, meaning "to make efforts so that it can be realized if at all possible."

examples: I can never thank him enough for his kindness.
I can't regret enough not having studied harder when I was a student.
If I lose here, I could not die in peace.
fields.explain: Uses the same verb twice to intensify its meaning. For example, 1. emphasizes deep gratitude, and 2. emphasizes strong regret. It is a somewhat idiomatic expression, and the verbs that can be used are limited. 「死んでも死にきれない」 is used as an emphatic expression of "cannot give up" or "to regret."

fields.name: Ｖ－ばいい（advice）
examples: If you want to rest, just rest.
If you don't have money, why not just borrow some from your dad?

Ａ: What should I do to lose weight?
Ｂ: Why not just eat less and exercise a lot?

Ａ: Around what time should we go?
Ｂ: As long as you come by 10 o'clock, that's fine.
fields.explain: An expression for recommending or suggesting that the other person take a particular action. Used when giving or asking for advice about what method or means is best to obtain a particular good result. It is similar in meaning to 「たらいい」 and can mostly replace it, but 「ばいい」 strongly carries the meaning "doing just that is necessary and sufficient." Depending on the context, it may carry a careless nuance, such as that the matter does not concern the speaker, or "don't you even understand something that simple?" When asking for advice, you either state the goal explicitly as in ３ａ, in the form 「どうすればやせられるか」, or use the question 「どうすればいいか」.

fields.meaning: To be careful of…, watch out for…
examples: Please watch out for cars.
Take care of your health and do your best.
Watch your language.

fields.meaning: I'm afraid ~, there is a risk of ~ | Indicates the possibility that something bad may happen
examples: There is a risk of heavy rain from tomorrow afternoon.
There is a risk of fire, so please do not put plastic bottles by the window.
This medicine may cause side effects, so you must be careful.
If your attendance rate is poor, there is a risk you won't be able to renew your visa.
The wind was strong and there was a risk of the fire spreading, so residents in the area evacuated.
The police believe the criminal may have already fled the country.
fields.explain: Expresses the possibility that a bad result may occur in the future; usually used in written language or announcements.
fields.notes:
1) Easily confused with ～かもしれない.
→ ～おそれがある means “I'm afraid/there is a risk of”, a more serious degree.
2) Usually used in written language, announcements and warnings.
→ Often seen in news and safety documents.
3) Not used for minor matters or mild personal feelings.
→ If it is just a subjective worry, use another pattern depending on the context.
meaning_vi: There is a possibility that…, I'm afraid that…
explain: Formal style, used a lot in official announcements, newspapers, warning signs and safety instructions.
The second clause is usually a warning, request or advisory: ～ので注意してください／～を控えてください／～が見込まれます など.
Not used in everyday small talk; instead use ～かもしれない to talk about possibility in a neutral, casual way.
Can be combined with degree adverbs:十分に/強く/大いに +恐れがある (strong emphasis).
Negating the risk: ～恐れはない (affirming there is nothing to worry about).
examples: 1. 大雨の影響で、川が氾濫する恐れがある。
Due to heavy rain, there is a risk of the river flooding.
2. この薬は眠気を催す恐れがあるため、運転は控えてください。
This medicine may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving.
3. 個人情報が第三者に漏れる恐れがあるため、速やかにパスワードを変更してください。
There is a risk of personal information leaking to third parties, so change your password immediately.
4. 設備の老朽化により、稼働を続けると事故の恐れがある。
Due to aging equipment, there is a risk of an accident if operation continues.
5. 地震の際は、落下物でけがをする恐れがあるので、机の下に避難してください。
During an earthquake, there is a risk of injury from falling objects, so take shelter under a desk.
6. 今回の遅れは全体のスケジュールに影響を及ぼす恐れがある。
This delay may affect the entire schedule. meaning_vi: There is a worry that　～, I'm afraid ～ ⏐ explain: Expresses that a situation is heading in a bad direction.
Formal sentence. ⏐ examples: 1. 地震の際には、窓ガラスが割れたり壁が倒れたりする恐れがある。
During an earthquake, I'm afraid window glass may break and walls may collapse.
2. 台風１９号は今夜、四国に上陸の恐れがあります。
I'm afraid Typhoon No. 19 may make landfall on Shikoku tonight.
mistakes: Using it for a positive result → Wrong nuance. Use 可能性がある for neutral/positive.
Attaching it directly to an adjective → Incorrect. It must be Vる or Nの.
Using it in casual speech → Sounds too stiff. Change to ～かもしれない when appropriate.
Confusing it with ～かねない: ～恐れがある is more formal/objective; ～かねない carries a subjective, emotional evaluation.
